## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

3	/// The Volume section's loudness half (spec §11 AU-15): the Loudness and At
4	/// volume readouts and the Normalize row's mode and target. The readout reads
5	/// through the pane's `loudnessMemo` (`ClipLoudness.Memo`), so a live Volume
6	/// or Pan drag reads no file and decodes no plan per tick; At volume is the
7	/// held answer plus the current base volume, through `AudioLimiterModel` while
8	/// the clip's limiter is on (AU-26) — on a clip with a stage the cache leaves
9	/// out, the last processed R0 or "≈" the cache figure (AU-64 (g)). Mode and
10	/// target are app-wide (`NormalizeChoice`), never an edit, so neither writes
11	/// the document.
12	extension AudioPane {
13	
14	    /// The one clip the readout is about: exactly one selected clip Normalize
15	    /// is offered for, else nothing ("—").
16	    private var readoutClip: UInt32? {
17	        let clips = AudioPane.normalizable(binding)
18	        return clips.count == 1 && binding.clips.count == 1 ? clips[0].id : nil
19	    }
20	
21	    private func loudnessAnswer() -> ClipLoudness.Answer {
22	        guard let clip = readoutClip, let document = binding.document else { return .unavailable }
23	        return loudnessMemo.answer(for: clip, in: document)
24	    }
25	
26	    /// "−41.7 LUFS · −18.5 dBTP", "measuring…" or "—"; `gain` in dB is added
27	    /// to both (At volume). With `limiter`, the loudness is the model's at that
28	    /// gain and the peak is held at the limiter's ceiling (AU-24, AU-26).
29	    private func loudnessText(gain: Double, limiter: LimiterProps? = nil) -> String {
30	        switch loudnessAnswer() {
31	        case .pending: return "measuring…"
32	        case .unavailable: return "—"
33	        case .reading(let reading):
34	            return levelText(
35	                lufs: reading.lufs, truePeak: reading.truePeak, steps: reading.steps,
36	                peaks: reading.stepPeaks, gain: gain, limiter: limiter)
37	        }
38	    }
39	
40	    /// One reading's figures at `gain` dB, through `limiter` when there is one.
41	    private func levelText(
42	        lufs measured: Double?, truePeak: Double, steps: [Double], peaks: [Double], gain: Double,
43	        limiter: LimiterProps?
44	    ) -> String {
45	        guard gain.isFinite else { return "silent" }
46	        var peak = truePeak > 0 ? 20 * log10(truePeak) + gain : -.infinity
47	        var lufs = measured.map { $0 + gain }
48	        if let limiter, measured != nil {
49	            let ceiling = pow(10, limiter.ceilingDb / 20)
50	            peak = min(peak, limiter.ceilingDb)
51	            lufs = AudioLimiterModel.integrated(
52	                steps: steps, peaks: peaks, gain: pow(10, gain / 20), ceiling: ceiling,
53	                releaseSeconds: Double(limiter.release) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
54	        }
55	        let peakText = peak.isFinite ? String(format: "%.1f dBTP", peak) : "−∞ dBTP"
56	        guard let lufs else { return "— LUFS · " + minus(peakText) }
57	        return minus(String(format: "%.1f LUFS · ", lufs) + peakText)
58	    }
59	
60	    /// At volume (spec §11 AU-64 (g)): on a clip whose chain has a stage the
61	    /// loudness cache leaves out, the last R0 measured for its plan and chain
62	    /// (`ProcessedLoudness.Memo`) at the current volume and limiter, else the
63	    /// cache figure marked approximate; any other clip, the cache figure.
64	    private func atVolumeText(_ audio: AudioProps) -> (text: String, approximate: Bool) {
65	        let cached = loudnessText(gain: audio.decibels, limiter: audio.limiter)
66	        guard ProcessedLoudness.needsRender(audio), let clip = readoutClip,
67	            let document = binding.document, case .reading = loudnessAnswer()
68	        else { return (cached, false) }
69	        guard let processed = ProcessedLoudness.Memo.shared.reading(for: clip, in: document) else {
70	            return ("≈ " + cached, true)
71	        }
72	        let text = levelText(
73	            lufs: StepLoudness.integrated(processed.steps), truePeak: processed.peaks.max() ?? 0,
74	            steps: processed.steps, peaks: processed.peaks, gain: audio.decibels,
75	            limiter: audio.limiter)
76	        return (text, false)
77	    }
78	
79	    static let approximateTip =
80	        "≈ before the clip's processing; Normalize or Enhance Voice measures through it."
81	
82	    private func minus(_ text: String) -> String {
83	        text.replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
84	    }

86	    /// The Loudness row (the clip's material at volume 1, pre-fader) and the
87	    /// At volume row (the same with the base volume's gain, through the
88	    /// clip's limiter when it has one).
89	    func loudnessRows() -> [NSView] {
90	        let binding = self.binding
91	        weak var atVolume: OptionDisplayControl?
92	        let readout = inspectorReadout(width: 160) { [weak self] in
93	            guard let self else { return "—" }
94	            let answer = self.atVolumeText(binding.audioProps)
95	            atVolume?.toolTip = answer.approximate ? AudioPane.approximateTip : nil
96	            return answer.text
97	        }
98	        atVolume = readout
99	        return [
100	            inspectorRow(
101	                "Loudness", [inspectorReadout(width: 160) { [weak self] in
102	                    self?.loudnessText(gain: 0) ?? "—"
103	                }]),
104	            inspectorRow("At volume", [readout]),
105	        ]
106	    }
107	
108	    /// The Normalize row: Mode (Peak | Loudness) and Target (LUFS, −50…−5,
109	    /// quick −14, −16, −23; live only in Loudness). A change re-titles
110	    /// `button`'s tooltip and refreshes the pane.
111	    func normalizeRow(updating button: OptionButtonControl) -> NSView {
112	        button.toolTip = AudioPane.normalizeTip()
113	        let modes = AudioNormalize.Mode.allCases
114	        let popup = OptionPopupControl(
115	            width: 96, items: ["Peak", "Loudness"],
116	            read: { modes.firstIndex(of: NormalizeChoice.mode) ?? 0 },
117	            write: { [weak self, weak button] index in
118	                NormalizeChoice.mode = modes[max(0, min(index, modes.count - 1))]
119	                button?.toolTip = AudioPane.normalizeTip()
120	                self?.inspector?.refresh(isLive: false)
121	            },
122	            enabled: { true }, onEdit: {})
123	        let range = AudioNormalize.targetLUFSRange
124	        let target = OptionFieldControl(
125	            width: InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth, unit: "LUFS", decimals: 1,
126	            min: range.lowerBound, max: range.upperBound,
127	            quick: AudioNormalize.targetLUFSQuickPicks,
128	            read: { NormalizeChoice.targetLUFS },
129	            write: { [weak self, weak button] value in
130	                NormalizeChoice.targetLUFS = min(max(value, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound)
131	                button?.toolTip = AudioPane.normalizeTip()
132	                self?.inspector?.refresh(isLive: false)
133	            },
134	            enabled: { NormalizeChoice.mode == .loudness }, onEdit: {})
135	        return inspectorRow("Normalize", [popup, target])
136	    }
137	
138	    /// The button's tooltip in the chosen mode. Two of the sentences are the
139	    /// limits, and they are here because this is where somebody meets them:
140	    /// the tool's description says the same things (road map 2 phase 5c,
141	    /// D-C3). The nest clause is a limit turned around: a nest alone leaves
142	    /// the button disabled, but a nest picked BESIDE an ordinary clip leaves it
143	    /// enabled and the nest quietly not asked about.
144	    static func normalizeTip() -> String {
145	        let rest =
146	            ". It REPLACES the volume rather than adding to it, so pressing it twice "
147	            + "changes nothing; it writes the clip's base level even while the playhead "
148	            + "is inside an action; and it leaves Mute alone. A nest is skipped: its "
149	            + "level lives in the clips inside it, not in the nest."
150	        switch NormalizeChoice.mode {
151	        case .peak:
152	            let level = String(format: "%.0f dBFS", AudioNormalize.defaultPeakDB)
153	            return "Set each selected clip's volume so its loudest moment reaches "
154	                + level.replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−") + rest
155	        case .loudness:
156	            let target = String(format: "%.1f LUFS", NormalizeChoice.targetLUFS)
157	            let ceiling = String(format: "%.0f dBTP", AudioNormalize.ceilingDBTP)
158	            return ("Set each selected clip's volume so its integrated loudness reaches " + target
159	                + ", turning the clip's limiter on at " + ceiling + " where its true peak would "
160	                + "pass it, and stopping short where the volume would pass "
161	                + AudioNormalize.maxGainName)
162	                .replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−") + rest
163	        }
164	    }
165	}

3	/// The volume line on the timeline (road map "audio" AP8a, spec §11
4	/// AU-81…AU-84): every clip with sound draws its envelope — the plan's ramps
5	/// through `VolumeLines`, on `VolumeScale` — over its waveform; a press on it
6	/// drags the level in force, ⌥-press adds a point. The model is
7	/// `VolumeLine.swift`.
8	///
9	/// Extensions in a file of their own, as the speech duck's line is
10	/// (`TimelineView+DuckCurve.swift`): `TimelineView.swift` is frozen at wiring
11	/// and keeps one call in `hit(at:)` and one arm in each gesture phase.
12	
13	/// One clip's line as drawn and hit: its rect, the scale on it, the ramps,
14	/// the polyline's vertices and the points (action ends naming the volume).
15	struct VolumeLineGeometry {
16	    let rect: CGRect
17	    let scale: VolumeScale
18	    let ramps: [PlanRamp]
19	    let vertices: [CGPoint]
20	    let points: [CGPoint]
21	}
22	
23	extension TimelineContentView {
24	    /// The shortest line rect drawn (AU-81).
25	    static let volumeLineMinHeight: CGFloat = 12
26	    /// How far from the line a press still takes it (AU-84).
27	    static let volumeLineReach: CGFloat = 3
28	
29	    /// The line on `clip` in lane rect `rect`: the audio region with its top
30	    /// raised to the action lane's bottom where they overlap, at least 12 pt
31	    /// tall, on a clip with sound that is not a nest clip and has an audio
32	    /// segment in the plan; nil otherwise. The drawing and the hit test both
33	    /// read this, so they cannot disagree.
34	    func volumeLineGeometry(
35	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, owner: TimelineView
36	    ) -> VolumeLineGeometry? {
37	        guard clip.source.nestID == nil, owner.hasAudio(clip),
38	              let ramps = owner.volumeLines?.ramps(for: clip.id)
39	        else { return nil }
40	        let content = Self.contentRect(rect)
41	        var audio = Self.regions(in: content, hasVideo: owner.hasVideo(clip), hasAudio: true).audio
42	        let lane = Self.actionLane(content: content, sizeIndex: owner.trackHeightIndex)
43	        if lane.height > 0, lane.maxY > audio.minY, lane.minY < audio.maxY {
44	            audio = CGRect(
45	                x: audio.minX, y: lane.maxY, width: audio.width,
46	                height: max(audio.maxY - lane.maxY, 0))
47	        }
48	        guard audio.height >= Self.volumeLineMinHeight, audio.width > 1 else { return nil }
49	        let scale = VolumeScale(rect: audio.insetBy(dx: 0, dy: 1))
50	        let layout = owner.layout
51	        var vertices: [CGPoint] = []
52	        for ramp in ramps {
53	            vertices.append(CGPoint(x: layout.x(for: ramp.start), y: scale.y(gain: ramp.from)))
54	            vertices.append(CGPoint(
55	                x: layout.x(for: ramp.start + ramp.duration), y: scale.y(gain: ramp.to)))
56	        }
57	        var points: [CGPoint] = []
58	        for action in clip.actions
59	        where action.end.audio?.volume != nil && action.endTime <= clip.duration {
60	            let t = clip.start + action.endTime
61	            guard let gain = VolumeLines.gain(at: t, in: ramps) else { continue }
62	            points.append(CGPoint(x: layout.x(for: t), y: scale.y(gain: gain)))
63	        }
64	        return VolumeLineGeometry(
65	            rect: audio, scale: scale, ramps: ramps, vertices: vertices, points: points)
66	    }
67	
68	    /// The line, its points and — while it is dragged — the readout. Called
69	    /// after the speech duck's line, inside the clip body's clip.
70	    func drawVolumeLine(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, owner: TimelineView, visible: CGRect) {
71	        guard let geometry = volumeLineGeometry(clip, rect: rect, owner: owner),
72	              geometry.vertices.count >= 2
73	        else { return }
74	        let from = max(geometry.rect.minX, visible.minX) - 1
75	        let to = min(geometry.rect.maxX, visible.maxX) + 1
76	        guard to > from else { return }
77	        // Each ramp is one leg; a leg wholly off screen is skipped and the
78	        // next drawn one starts a new subpath, so a long clip costs only what
79	        // shows. Consecutive legs share their end and start points.
80	        let path = NSBezierPath()
81	        var open = false
82	        for leg in stride(from: 0, to: geometry.vertices.count - 1, by: 2) {
83	            let a = geometry.vertices[leg]
84	            let b = geometry.vertices[leg + 1]
85	            guard b.x >= from, a.x <= to else {
86	                open = false
87	                continue
88	            }
89	            if open { path.line(to: a) } else { path.move(to: a) }
90	            path.line(to: b)
91	            open = true
92	        }
93	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
94	        NSBezierPath(rect: geometry.rect).addClip()
95	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.85).setStroke()
96	        path.lineWidth = 1
97	        path.stroke()
98	        DS.action.setFill()
99	        for point in geometry.points where point.x >= from && point.x <= to {
100	            NSRect(x: point.x - 2.5, y: point.y - 2.5, width: 5, height: 5).fill()
101	        }
102	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
103	        if let drag = owner.volumeDrag, drag.clip == clip.id {
104	            drawVolumeReadout(VolumeLine.readout(drag.volume), at: drag.point, in: geometry.rect)
105	        }
106	    }
107	
108	    /// The dragged value beside the pointer, kept inside the line's rect
109	    /// where it fits.
110	    private func drawVolumeReadout(_ text: String, at point: CGPoint, in rect: CGRect) {
111	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
112	            .font: NSFont.monospacedDigitSystemFont(ofSize: 10, weight: .medium),
113	            .foregroundColor: NSColor.white,
114	        ]
115	        let size = (text as NSString).size(withAttributes: attributes)
116	        var chip = CGRect(
117	            x: point.x + 8, y: point.y - size.height - 6, width: size.width + 8,
118	            height: size.height + 2)
119	        if chip.maxX > rect.maxX { chip.origin.x = point.x - 8 - chip.width }
120	        chip.origin.y = min(max(chip.minY, rect.minY), max(rect.maxY - chip.height, rect.minY))
121	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.7).setFill()
122	        chip.fill()
123	        (text as NSString).draw(
124	            at: CGPoint(x: chip.minX + 4, y: chip.minY + 1), withAttributes: attributes)
125	    }
126	
127	    /// AU-84: within the line's rect and 3 pt of the line at the pointer's x,
128	    /// the clip and the press's project time. `hit(at:)` asks after the fade
129	    /// handles, the action band and the edge grabs, and before the clip body.
130	    func volumeLineHit(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, rect: CGRect, at point: CGPoint) -> TimelineHit? {
131	        guard let owner = timeline,
132	              let geometry = volumeLineGeometry(clip, rect: rect, owner: owner),
133	              geometry.rect.contains(point)
134	        else { return nil }
135	        let time = owner.layout.time(atX: point.x)
136	        guard let gain = VolumeLines.gain(at: time, in: geometry.ramps),
137	              abs(point.y - geometry.scale.y(gain: gain)) <= Self.volumeLineReach
138	        else { return nil }
139	        return .volumeLine(clip.id, time)
140	    }
141	}
142	
143	extension TimelineView {
144	    /// The `.volumeLine` arm, after the frozen file has selected the clip: a
145	    /// plain press drags the level in force (AU-82), ⌥ adds a point first
146	    /// (AU-83) — at once, so a click alone adds it — or beeps where one
147	    /// cannot go.
148	    func beginVolumeLine(_ id: UInt32, at point: CGPoint, time: Ticks, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags) {
149	        guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id),
150	              let index = snapshot.tracks.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == clip.track }),
151	              let geometry = content.volumeLineGeometry(

153	                  owner: self)

161	            else {
162	                NSSound.beep()

164	            }

169	            volumeDrag = session

171	            onLiveUpdate?(session.ops)
172	        } else {
173	            let target = VolumeLine.target(of: clip, at: clipTime)
174	            volumeDrag = VolumeLineSession(
175	                clip: id, target: target, prefix: [], pressY: point.y, scale: geometry.scale,
176	                volume: target.volume, point: point)
177	            onLiveBegin?()
178	        }
179	    }

181	    /// Vertical only: the pointer's y against the press's, on the scale the
182	    /// press found.
183	    func continueVolumeLine(at point: CGPoint) {
184	        guard var session = volumeDrag else { return }
185	        session.update(y: point.y)
186	        session.point = point
187	        volumeDrag = session
188	        onLiveUpdate?(session.ops)
189	    }

191	    /// One undo step, "Set Volume" or "Add Volume Point"; none when nothing
192	    /// changed (`ProjectDocument.endLiveEdit`).
193	    func endVolumeLine() {
194	        guard let session = volumeDrag else { return }
195	        volumeDrag = nil
196	        onLiveEnd?(session.undoName)
197	    }

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `cursor_file.rs` — the cursor file, format v1 (road map "creator-jobs" CU1a, spec
  §11 CU-10): its module doc IS the format's specification (the header, the columns
  in integer µs and points × 100, the caps, every refusal's sentence, the parse
  order); `RC_CURSOR_FILE_VERSION` (the header's `#define` held to it by
  `core/tests/cursor_file.rs`), the caps, the types and `CursorFile::parse`, which
  reads the object, `format`, `version` and CU-7's `typed` keys loosely BEFORE the
  strict `deny_unknown_fields` read through `serde_path_to_error`, so a newer file is
  refused by its version and a project by its format. `cursor_file_check.rs` — its
  check (`check`, `check_typed`; a shortcut holds `cmd` or `ctrl`, or `opt` with
  `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS`, CU-60) and the base64 decoder, a module of its own because
  the two together pass the 400-line cap for a new file. `ffi_cursor.rs` —
  `rc_cursor_open` (parse and check; an open is the recorder's read-back, CU-15),
  `rc_cursor_free` and `rc_cursor_query` (road map creator-jobs CU2, spec §11 CU-25).
  `cursor_track.rs` — `CursorTrack`, the handle: the parsed file and its prepared
  paths under a `Mutex` (a `state` holds it only to clone an `Arc`, a poisoned lock
  taken with `into_inner`), ticks ↔ µs through `time.rs`, CU-20's M2 mapping per
  geometry entry (`scale_factor`, not `pixels_per_point`; `to_movie`, the one function), the raw path, idle opacity (CU-22),
  the image in force and ripples (CU-23). `cursor_smooth.rs` — `hold_end`, the one
  hold rule, and `SmoothPath` (pins, RDP, centripetal Catmull–Rom; CU-21).
  `cursor_query.rs` — the request vocabulary (its module doc) and `query`.
  `cursor_query_reads.rs` — its `events` and `path` reads, a pure move out of it (road map
  creator-jobs CU11a's toll); `state` takes `ends` and answers the shutter's two positions (spec
  §11 CU-115).
  `cursor_bursts.rs` — typing stretches and scroll bursts, one run finder. Auto Zoom's
  planner (road map creator-jobs CU7, spec §11 CU-70…CU-75), `plan_zooms` in
  `rc_cursor_query` (one track per clip, and the project): `cursor_zoom.rs` its
  arguments, refusals in CU-75's order, Replace's removals (`is_zoom` only), the bases a
  hold across a cut sets, and the ops (`remove_action`, `set_video`, `add_zoom_action` in
  time order) and answer; `cursor_zoom_run.rs` a run (clips continuing one source on one
  track) — its anchors through S, scroll bursts, barriers, the 10 Hz follow cursor and
  `land` (only given clips, no straddled cut); `cursor_zoom_visits.rs` anchors → visits →
  planned actions in container time, pure. Add Shortcut Overlays' planner (road map
  creator-jobs CU8, spec §11 CU-80…CU-84), `plan_overlays` in `rc_cursor_query` (one track per
  clip, and the project): `cursor_overlays.rs` — its arguments and refusals, the presses through
  `cursor_zoom_run.rs`'s `media_in` and `clip_time`, CU-80's timing in grid frames
  (`min_frames`, D_min(n) = 10n + 25; the same chord merged as "×k"; a different chord more than
  0.5 s late dropped), CU-83's Shortcuts track rule (`TRACK_NAME`; the front-most one in front of
  every given clip's track, unlocked, shown, no matte, free over the span, else a new one at the
  front with `next_id`) and the `add_track` / `add_graphic_clip` ops. Speed Up Typing's
  planner (road map creator-jobs CU9b, spec §11 CU-91, CU-92), `plan_typing` in
  `rc_cursor_query` (one track per clip, and the project): `cursor_typing.rs` — its arguments
  and refusals (rate ×2–×8, shortest 1–30 s, then per clip; reversed refused), each typing
  stretch clamped to the played window through `clip_time`, less every speech span of a media
  clip with sound under it (`speech_in_clip`) and each recorded press's overlay span
  (Shortcuts-track clips holding it or starting within `MOST_LATE`, else `DEFAULT_DURATION`,
  both `cursor_overlays.rs`'s; presses not filtered by `[from, to)`), every clip's pieces
  united (touching merged) before `shortest` and the 0.3 s margins, `needs_speech` when a
  counted media has no `speech`, and the `retime_range` ops right to left, tried in order on a
  clone (all or nothing). `encode_base64`
  sits beside `decode_base64` in `cursor_file_check.rs`, base64's one home. No file
  I/O, no pixel work: a PNG is checked by its signature.
- `model_cursor.rs` · `cursor_props.rs` · `recipe_cursor.rs` — the cursor in the model and the
  recipe (format 38, road map "creator-jobs" CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-32, CU-35, CU-39):
  `model_cursor.rs` `MediaCursor` (`media.cursor`, after `speech`, written only when set,
  `in_picture` required) and `CursorProps` (`video.cursor`, after `look`, written only when set,
  every field written, `{}` the defaults) with `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` and the `CURSOR_*`
  ranges, re-exported through `model_props.rs`; `cursor_props.rs` `check_cursor` (one line in
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_video`), `clamp_cursor` (one line in `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_video`; it never fails, so the video group always decodes), `check_media_cursor`
  (`check_media_fields`' last check) and `with_base_cursor`, the one statement that `smoothing`
  and `hide_idle` are the clip's BASE values — read by `recipe_cursor.rs`, `edit_split.rs`'s
  second half and `freeze_frame`'s still; `recipe_cursor.rs` `Project::layer_cursor`, a layer's
  `cursor` key: `null` unless a media or still clip's media has a cursor not `in_picture` and the
  evaluated props show or ripple, else `{media, at, reversed, smoothing, hide_idle, props}`, `at`
  `freeze_frame`'s source tick in the stream the clip plays.
- `model_cutout.rs` · `cutout_check.rs` — the cutout in the model (format 39, road map
  "creator-jobs" CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21, CO-23): `model_cutout.rs` `Cutout`
  (`video.cutout`, after `cursor`, written only when set, every field written, `{}` the
  defaults) with `CutoutSubject` (`person`, and `foreground`, format 41, road map creator-jobs
  CO10a, spec §11 CO-100), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground` and the `CUTOUT_*` ranges,
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; `cutout_check.rs` `check_cutout` (one line in
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_video`: edge, feather, then `best` refused), `check_cutout_clip` (one
  line in `edit_props.rs`'s `settle_video`: a media, still or image clip takes one, a text, shape,
  graphic, adjustment or nest clip refused naming what it is, then `foreground` refused on a media
  or still clip in its own sentence, CO-100), `check_behind_subject_clip` (one line in `settle_video` after it:
  `video.behind_subject`, format 40, spec §11 CO-52, refused on an adjustment or nest clip),
  `clamp_cutout` (one line in `actions_clamp.rs`'s `clamp_video`; it
  never fails) and `restore_base_cutout` (through `restore_base_video_keys`, one line in
  `actions.rs`'s `evaluate_clip`, beside motion's restore: the presence, `subject` and `quality`
  the base's). The recipe's `cutout` key
  is `recipe_layer.rs`'s `Project::layer_cutout`: `null` unless a media, still or image clip's media
  is in the project and the evaluated cutout is set, else `{mask: {kind: "media", media, quality},
  background, edge, feather}`, `media` the clip's own source media; an image clip's mask is
  `{kind: "image", media, subject, quality}` (CO-101), drawn uncut until CO10b. `add_blurred_background`'s
  copy drops it. `VideoProps.behind_subject` (format 40, after `cutout`, written only when true)
  is `model_props.rs`'s; the copy drops it too. `cutout_check.rs` also holds hide while
  silent's checks (format 43, spec §11 CO-92): `check_hide_silent`,
  `Project::check_hide_silent_clip` and `restore_base_video_keys` (`video_gate.rs`'s entry).
- `motion_blur.rs` · `recipe_blur.rs` — motion blur (format 42, road map "creator-jobs"
  CU11a, spec §11 CU-110…CU-114): `motion_blur.rs` `MOTION_BLUR_SAMPLES` (CU-S5's N, 16),
  `check_motion_blur` (one line in `check_video`), `clamp_motion_blur` (one line in
  `clamp_video`), `check_motion_blur_clip` (one line in `settle_video`: a nest or adjustment
  clip refused above 0) and `shutter_offsets` (the N centred offsets and the two ends, on the
  canvas's frame); `recipe_blur.rs` `Shutter`, `Project::layer_shutter` (none at 0 or when
  `layer`'s `sharp` holds: drawn into, a matte, a transition, a dissolve, a shadow, an
  adjustment clip; times clamped into the instance's span), `Project::layer_blur` (the layer's
  `blur` key from `placement` at each time, `null` when every sample equals the first) and
  `sharpen_matted` (after `frame_subjects`: every matted layer's `blur` null and its cursor's
  `shutter` removed). `VideoProps.motion_blur` (after `behind_subject`, written only above 0)
  is `model_props.rs`'s; `video_json` always carries it; `add_blurred_background`'s copy drops
  it. `recipe_cursor.rs`'s `layer_cursor` takes the shutter's ends and appends `shutter
  {from, to, samples}`.
- `video_gate.rs` — hide while silent (format 43, road map "creator-jobs" CO9, spec §11
  CO-90…CO-93): `Project::hide_silent_gate` (an instance's gate at a tick: the nearest container,
  outward from the layer's own, in which an instance of the media covers it; there, the instances
  whose played window meets `[t − hold − fade, t + pre_roll + fade]`, each projected at its own
  origin through `audio_duck_speech.rs`'s `played_speech`, sorted and `widened`; the maximum of 1
  inside and a ramp to 0 over `fade`, a step at 0; 1 with no gate, no saved speech or no covering
  instance), multiplied into `recipe.rs`'s `layer` only (`clip_state`, `placement` and every edit
  read un-gated); `gate_entries` (the plan's `gates`, one per timeline-level gated instance, after
  `ducks`, only when non-empty, each instance's ramps windowed as the gate is); `clear_hide_silent`
  (`remove_media`'s non-LUT arm, timeline and every nest); `hide_silent_media` (paste's non-shown
  media list, `keep_range`'s kept media) and `remap_hide_silent` (an id the map lacks drops the
  gate, `remap_look_media`'s rule). `HideSilent` (`media`, `pre_roll`, `hold`, `fade`, all
  written; `HIDE_SILENT_PRE_ROLL`, `_HOLD`, `_FADE`, `_MAX`) and `VideoProps.hide_silent` (after
  `motion_blur`, written only when set) are `model_props.rs`'s; `check_hide_silent` (one line in
  `check_video`), `Project::check_hide_silent_clip` (one line in `settle_video`: media named, in
  the project, with sound, then a nest clip refused) and `restore_base_video_keys` (`actions.rs`'
  one call: the cutout's restore and the base's whole `hide_silent`) are `cutout_check.rs`'s;
  `not_a_target` refuses `video.hide_silent` in a patch and in `off`.
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

---
title: "How audio works"
description: Where sound lives in a project, the order it passes through a clip's settings, what a nest and a track do to it, and which tool to reach for.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every clip with sound is mixed by its own settings and then by its track's. This page is the map: where sound lives, the order it's processed in, and which page covers each job.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The timeline', 'Clip tab ▸ Sound', 'The track header']}
  tools={['set_audio', 'set_track']}
/>

## One kind of track for all sound

Frame Job has no separate audio tracks. Any track can hold a clip with sound:

- a video file
- an audio-only file, such as a voice-over, music or a recorder's take
- a microphone recording
- a clip split off with [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
- a [nest](/editing/nests/) that holds sound

Each clip has its own processing on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). Each track can be [muted or soloed](/audio/mute-and-solo/) and has its own [volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/), [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).

The preview and the export use the same mix, so what you hear while editing is what gets written. There are two exceptions:

- Every export also holds its peaks under −1 dBTP with a master limiter the preview doesn't have. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
- A track's compressor and limiter are exact in an export and approximate in the preview. See [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).

## Clip waveforms

A clip with sound shows its waveform in the timeline, below the filmstrip when it has both. The waveform is the file's own level, so moving the **Volume** slider doesn't redraw it. The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) over it shows what you actually hear.

The waveform is drawn faded when the clip is muted, when its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track holding only sound clips is drawn as a shorter lane than a track with pictures. [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) covers everything a clip draws.

## The fixed signal order

Sound passes through a clip's settings in one fixed order. You can't rearrange it. The order matters because each stage hears what the one before it left: the compressor's threshold, for example, is read against sound the noise reducer has already cleaned.

1. [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
2. [Voice Effect](/audio/voice-effects/)
3. [Channels](/audio/channels/)
4. [EQ](/audio/eq/)
5. [Hum](/audio/hum-removal/)
6. [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
7. [Gate](/audio/gate/)
8. [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
9. [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
10. [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
11. [Mix](/audio/pan-and-mono/): Mix to mono, then Pan
12. [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
13. [Volume](/audio/volume/), [fades](/audio/fades/) and [ducking](/audio/ducking/)

The last step works like a fader. Those three are the first sections on the Sound tab, because they're what you reach for most, but they're applied last. The other sections read down the tab in signal order.

The limiter is told the clip's **Volume**, so its ceiling holds at the level you set, even though Volume comes after it in the list.

## Sound on a nest

A nest clip has the same Sound tab, but most of the controls don't reach the clips inside it.

| On a nest clip | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Volume**, **Mute** and the fades | Scale everything inside. Turning a nest down turns all of it down, and muting it silences all of it. |
| **Mix to mono** | Folds the nest's whole mix. Pans on the tracks inside it no longer apply. |
| **Ducking** | Lowers the rest of the project for the nest's whole length. |
| Pan, Channels, EQ, Hum, Gate, Leveller, De-esser, Compressor, Voice Isolation, Voice Effect, Noise Reduction and Limiter | Nothing. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set them on the clips inside. |

A nest clip draws no [volume line](/audio/volume-line/), and [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) pass over it, because its level lives in the clips inside. Alone in the selection it leaves both buttons disabled. Beside an ordinary clip, the ordinary clip is processed and the nest is skipped.

## What a track adds

A track acts as a bus for its clips. Its volume, pan, compressor and limiter work on everything on it, after each clip's own settings.

A clip inside a nest plays through its own track in the nest and then through the track the nest clip sits on. Track volumes and pans multiply along the way, so a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left. A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter, only volume and pan.

## Sound analysis after import

Frame Job analyses each file's sound on your Mac after import, with no key and no upload: first its waveform, then its loudness, then what Synchronize Audio matches on, and then where its speech is. Until that finishes:

- The clip has no waveform yet.
- The **Loudness** read-out says "measuring…".
- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) skips the clip.
- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) skip it, naming it as "still being analysed".
- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) stops and says the clip "is still being analysed".

Try again in a moment. Nothing needs starting by hand.

## Find the right tool

| To | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Set how loud a clip plays | [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) |
| Change the level over time | [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) or [actions](/audio/animate-sound/) |
| Bring clips to one loudness | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
| Clean up a voice recording in one step | [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) |
| Make one clip sound like another | [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) |
| Drop the music under a voice | [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) or [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) |
| Line up a camera and a separate recorder | [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) |
| Move sound to its own clip, or make a J-cut | [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/), [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) |
| Give many clips the same treatment | [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies the whole sound setup in one step |
| Cut out dead air | [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) |
| Check a mix by ear and by number | [The level meter](/audio/level-meter/) and [the Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) |

## Related

- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)
- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)
- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)

---
title: "The Sound tab"
description: The Clip tab's Sound sub-tab, its fifteen sections, and how to read, reset and edit them across several clips.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Sound tab is where you set how a clip plays: how loud it is, how it's cleaned up and where it sits in the mix.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound" tools={['set_audio', 'get_project']} />

<Shot
  name="09-clip-sound.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with an audio file selected and the Sound sub-tab chosen. The Volume section is open, showing Volume at 100%, Gain +0.0 dB, Loudness and At volume both −21.8 LUFS · −20.8 dBTP, Mute, the Normalize row set to Loudness at −16 LUFS, and the Normalize and Enhance Voice buttons. Below it the Fades section reads none, and Ducking and Voice Isolation read off."
/>

## When the tab appears

The Clip tab shows **Sound** when the selection includes at least one clip that plays sound. That means a clip whose file has an audio track with its sound switched on, or a nest that holds audio. A clip whose sound is [switched off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) doesn't count.

An audio-only clip has no picture, so the Clip tab opens straight on Sound. For a video clip, choose **Sound** beside **Picture**.

## The sections

Each section header shows a one-line summary of its state, so you can read a clip's setup with every section closed. The summary is drawn a little stronger when the section differs from its default.

| Section | What it's for | Its summary reads | **Reset** does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

---
title: "Clip volume"
description: Set how loud a clip plays, mute it, and read its gain, loudness and true peak in the Volume section.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Volume section sets a clip's level and tells you how loud the clip is before and after that level. It's the first section on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Volume" tools={['set_audio', 'normalize_clip']} />

<Shot
  name="09-clip-sound.inspector"
  alt="The Volume section open on the Sound tab: the Volume slider and a field at 100%, Gain +0.0 dB, Loudness and At volume both −21.8 LUFS · −20.8 dBTP, an unticked Mute box, the Normalize row, and the Normalize and Enhance Voice buttons."
/>

## Set the volume

Drag the **Volume** slider, type in its field, or choose a value from the field's chevron: 0, 50, 100, 150, 200 or 400 %.

| Control | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Volume** | 100 % | 0 to 3200 % (+30.1 dB) |

The slider stops at 400 %. To go higher, type in the field, up to 3200 %. Above 400 % the slider's knob stays at the right end. The high ceiling is there so that a quiet microphone recording can be lifted as far as it needs.

To change the level over the length of a clip, drag the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) on the timeline. With an [action selected](/audio/animate-sound/), **Volume** writes the level the action ends on, not the clip's own.

## Mute a clip

Tick **Mute** to silence the clip without changing its volume. It's off by default.

A muted clip's waveform is drawn faded and its [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) lies along the bottom. To silence a whole track, use [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).

With an action selected, **Mute** switches at the action's end, and the row shows "at end".

## Read the level

Three rows report the clip's level. You can't edit them.

### Gain

**Gain** is the **Volume** in decibels, such as "+3.0 dB", or "silent" at 0 %. At 100 % it reads "+0.0 dB".

### Loudness

**Loudness** is the clip's integrated loudness and true peak at volume 100 %, such as "−41.7 LUFS · −18.5 dBTP". It's measured to BS.1770-4 over the part of the file the clip plays.

| It counts | It doesn't count |
| --- | --- |
| The channel choice, Mix to mono and Pan | Volume, fades, ducking, Mute and solo |
| A mono clip as dual mono, as an export plays it, which reads about 3 dB louder than the file alone | EQ, Hum and the rest of the clip's processing, and the track's volume |

A clip at another speed, or a ramped one, reads within about 0.5 LU of what plays. A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it.

### At volume

**At volume** is the same reading with the clip's **Volume** applied, and through its [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) when that's on. With the limiter on, the true peak reads no higher than the ceiling. The row follows a **Volume** drag as you move.

The fast reading can't hear EQ, Hum, Voice Isolation, Noise Reduction, the Gate, the Leveller, the De-esser, the Compressor or a Voice Effect. On a clip using any of them:

- If [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode or [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) has measured the clip as it is now, the row reads that measurement.
- Otherwise the figure is the one before the processing and starts with "≈". Its tooltip says so.

**At volume** doesn't measure on its own, so "≈" stays until you press one of those two.

### What the read-outs can show instead

| It reads | Because |
| --- | --- |
| "measuring…" | The clip's [sound analysis](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-analysis-after-import) hasn't finished. |
| "—" | Several clips are selected, or a nest is, or the clip can't be measured. |
| "— LUFS" beside a peak | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, or it's quieter than −70 LUFS throughout. |
| "silent" (At volume) | **Volume** is 0 %. |

## Reset the section

**Reset** in the section's header puts **Volume** back to 100 % and turns **Mute** off. It leaves the Normalize row alone, and it leaves the [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) alone, including one Normalize turned on.

## Good to know

- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) sit at the bottom of this section. Both set **Volume** for you, and both leave **Mute** alone.
- On a [nest clip](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-on-a-nest), **Volume** and **Mute** scale everything inside it.
- A muted clip that ducks still lowers the others. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).

## Related

- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)
- [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/)
- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)

---
title: "The volume line"
description: See a clip's level over time on the timeline, drag it, and add points to shape it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The volume line is the thin white line over a clip's waveform. It shows how loud that clip plays over time, and you can drag it to change the level without leaving the timeline.

<AtAGlance
  keys="⌥-click to add a point"
  where="On a clip's audio part in the timeline"
  tools={['set_audio', 'add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action']}
/>

## The line on a clip

Every clip with sound draws the line, except a nest clip. It's the level you hear from that clip, with everything that shapes it folded in:

- the clip's **Volume** and its volume actions
- its fades and crossfades
- ducking from other clips
- the track's volume

The top of the clip's audio part is +30 dB (3200 %) and the bottom is −60 dB or quieter. A clip at 100 % sits about a third of the way down.

A clip you can't hear has its line along the bottom. That's a muted clip, one on a muted track, or one silenced by another track's solo.

A small square in the action colour marks each action end that sets the volume. Those squares are the line's points.

The line starts below the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and is only drawn where the audio part is at least 12 pt tall, so at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) it may not show.

## Drag the line

Press within 3 pt of the line and drag up or down. The new level appears beside the pointer, such as "+2.5 dB", or "−∞ dB" at silence. One drag is one undo step, "Set Volume".

What the drag changes depends on where you press:

| You press | The drag changes |
| --- | --- |
| Inside an action that sets the volume | That action's end level |
| After such an action | The end level of the last one before the point |
| Anywhere else | The clip's own **Volume** |

The drag is vertical only and relative to where you pressed. It moves in decibels, and it covers the whole scale over the height of the audio part, so a taller [track](/timeline/track-height/) gives you finer control.

To go to silence, drag down to the very bottom of the audio part. The level stops at 3200 % at the top.

The readout is the level you're setting, not the sum on the line. The line includes track volume and ducking, but a drag changes only the clip's own level, so on a silenced clip the line stays on the floor while the readout changes.

## Add a point

A point lets the level change partway through a clip.

<Steps>

1. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> and click the line where you want the point.

2. Keep the mouse down and drag to set its level, or let go and drag the line later.

</Steps>

A point is an [action](/motion/actions/), not a keyframe. Frame Job adds an action running from the end of the previous action, or the clip's start, up to where you clicked, ending at the level the line already has there. The click on its own changes nothing you hear. It's one undo step, "Add Volume Point".

Inside an action that changes only the volume, the click splits that action in two at the point. Both halves keep its curve, so a linear action sounds the same until you drag, and an eased one eases again on each side of the point.

The click beeps and adds nothing:

- inside an action that changes anything besides the volume
- inside an action that runs past the clip's end, as one can after a trim
- within one frame of the start of the action it's in, or of the previous action's end

## Move or remove a point

To move a point in time, drag its action band. To remove one, select the band and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

## Clicks that reach the clip instead

Some presses on the line act on the clip, as they do anywhere else on it:

| Press | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click | Adds the clip to the selection or takes it out |
| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | Slips the clip |
| Double-click | Renames the clip |

The fade handles, the action lane and the clip's edges take a press before the line does.

## Good to know

- The line doesn't respond on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
- A clip with its [sound switched off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) draws no line, and neither does one playing [too fast to have sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
- Inside an open nest, the line is the nest's own mix. It doesn't include the volume, fades, mute or solo of the nest clip and the tracks outside it.

## With an agent

There's no separate tool for the line. A drag is `set_audio` or `set_action_end` on the action in force, and a point is `add_action` then `set_action_end`, with `set_action` when it splits an action. See [Tools: actions](/mcp/tools-actions/).

## Related

- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)
- [Audio fades](/audio/fades/)
- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)

The top of the clip's audio part is +30 dB (3200 %) and the bottom is −60 dB or quieter. A clip at 100 % sits about a third of the way down.

A clip you can't hear has its line along the bottom. That's a muted clip, one on a muted track, or one silenced by another track's solo.

A small square in the action colour marks each action end that sets the volume. Those squares are the line's points.

The line starts below the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and is only drawn where the audio part is at least 12 pt tall, so at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) it may not show.

## Drag the line

Press within 3 pt of the line and drag up or down. The new level appears beside the pointer, such as "+2.5 dB", or "−∞ dB" at silence. One drag is one undo step, "Set Volume".

What the drag changes depends on where you press:

| You press | The drag changes |
| --- | --- |
| Inside an action that sets the volume | That action's end level |
| After such an action | The end level of the last one before the point |
| Anywhere else | The clip's own **Volume** |

The drag is vertical only and relative to where you pressed. It moves in decibels, and it covers the whole scale over the height of the audio part, so a taller [track](/timeline/track-height/) gives you finer control.

To go to silence, drag down to the very bottom of the audio part. The level stops at 3200 % at the top.

The readout is the level you're setting, not the sum on the line. The line includes track volume and ducking, but a drag changes only the clip's own level, so on a silenced clip the line stays on the floor while the readout changes.

## Add a point

A point lets the level change partway through a clip.

<Steps>

1. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> and click the line where you want the point.

2. Keep the mouse down and drag to set its level, or let go and drag the line later.

</Steps>

A point is an [action](/motion/actions/), not a keyframe. Frame Job adds an action running from the end of the previous action, or the clip's start, up to where you clicked, ending at the level the line already has there. The click on its own changes nothing you hear. It's one undo step, "Add Volume Point".

Inside an action that changes only the volume, the click splits that action in two at the point. Both halves keep its curve, so a linear action sounds the same until you drag, and an eased one eases again on each side of the point.

The click beeps and adds nothing:

- inside an action that changes anything besides the volume
- inside an action that runs past the clip's end, as one can after a trim
- within one frame of the start of the action it's in, or of the previous action's end

## Move or remove a point

To move a point in time, drag its action band. To remove one, select the band and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

## Clicks that reach the clip instead

Some presses on the line act on the clip, as they do anywhere else on it:

| Press | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click | Adds the clip to the selection or takes it out |
| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | Slips the clip |
| Double-click | Renames the clip |

The fade handles, the action lane and the clip's edges take a press before the line does.

## Good to know

- The line doesn't respond on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
- A clip with its [sound switched off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) draws no line, and neither does one playing [too fast to have sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
- Inside an open nest, the line is the nest's own mix. It doesn't include the volume, fades, mute or solo of the nest clip and the tracks outside it.

## With an agent

There's no separate tool for the line. A drag is `set_audio` or `set_action_end` on the action in force, and a point is `add_action` then `set_action_end`, with `set_action` when it splits an action. See [Tools: actions](/mcp/tools-actions/).

## Related

- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)
- [Audio fades](/audio/fades/)
- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
